targetText: The value of every commodity produced in the capitalist way is represented in the formula: C = c + v + s. If we subtract surplus-values from this value of the product there remains a bare equivalent or a substitute value in goods, for the capital-value c + v expended in the elements of production.
explanation: Total commodity value equals constant capital (c) + variable capital (v) + surplus value (s). Capitalists measure cost price as (c + v) and view surplus value (s) as profit on their entire outlay.
